newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures bore the brunt of a surprise win for the opposition left in the first round of the parliamentary election while the French franc came under renewed pressure late in the day.

The respective June contracts slumped initially on GLOBEX, recovered ground as local traders bought back short positions, but then felt the weight of non-resident selling prior to the close with sentiment still nervous.
While domestic buyers buoyed the cash market, partly on the view European monetary union would be unhindered by a Socialist win some feared a wave of non-resident selling on Tuesday.

Traders said there had been heavy selling by local traders from the start of the GLOBEX session which knocked June PIBOR and the June bond future down to 96.12 and 128.00 respectively before they bought back later in the session.

Although many non-residents were present selling on Monday, some analysts said there was still concern the French market would come under further pressure when the United Kingdom and the United States come back from a long weekend on Tuesday.
Many traders said the market was still clinging to the belief the centre-right coalition would come through and retain power despite trailing in the first round.
"The market's very sanguine, it's still pricing in the odds (of a centre-right win) at 50/50," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance said.
Traders said cash-rich domestic investors took advantage of the rise in yields to snap up bonds and that the activity in the cash market calmed the futures market.

"We've seen people buying two-, five-, and 10-year paper on the sentiment that on European issues, the external disciplining force is very powerful...and they saw these spreads as being relatively attractive," a trader at a French bank said.

The 10-year spread narrowed to minus three basis points from minus 14 before the election but returned to minus 10 by the end of the session. There was a similar pattern at the two-year part of the curve. The spread widened to 37 basis points from 14 before stabilising around 28.
The franc fell with PIBOR early in the day, recovered to 3.3750 but slipped again on the back of non-resident selling late in the day to touch a low of 3.3784.
Traders said they did not expect the franc to fall much beyond 3.3820/25 and that the Bank of France would probably step in, discreetly, to prevent any sharp moves.
It was trading at 3.3771, after fairly heavy volume, at 1502 GMT. Traders said they had not seen or heard of the central bank stepping in to support the franc.
As expected the Bank of France left its key intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent at a regular money market tender.
The selloff at the short end, however, hit three-month yields at the Treasury's weekly auction. The average yield rose to 3.42 percent from 3.26 percent last week.
